summary.text: One of Penelope's suitors in Apollodorus' catalogue of the fifty-seven wooers from Dulichium — distinct from `agenor-zacynthus` in Epitome 7.29; a namesake of Agenor king of Phoenicia and of the Trojan Agenor who faced Achilles at the Scaean gate.

story.text: Apollodorus names Agenor among the suitors who devoured Odysseus' substance, listed after Clytius and before Eurypylus in the long company of Penelope's wooers.
The same name appears again among the wooers from Zacynthus in Epitome 7.29 — a homonym hazard; see `agenor-zacynthus`.
